title_en: Qiu Yuliang et al. v. People's Insurance Company of China Limited, Guanyun Branch, et al. — dispute over accidental injury insurance contract
ruling_gist_en: The teaching environment and activity facilities of a school must meet safety requirements to protect students' life and health from harm. If the student's right to life and health is damaged due to reasons attributable to the school, and the school should bear compensation liability under the campus liability insurance it has purchased, the insurance company shall compensate on behalf of the school in accordance with the insurance contract. If the school enters into a humanitarian assistance compensation agreement with the parents on condition of exempting its own liability, such agreement should be primarily recognized as compensatory in nature, rather than exempting the insurance company's compensation liability. When the school is negligent in claiming insurance compensation, the victim's right to claim insurance should not be deprived based on such agreement.
keywords_en: civil; insurance contract dispute; first instance; Basic People's Court; Jiangsu Province; natural person; legal person; Insurance Law; determination of school liability; validity of humanitarian compensation agreement; right to claim insurance; partial support; student sudden death while running; campus liability insurance; humanitarian compensation agreement; good faith; contract dispute; insurance contract; etc. accidental injury insurance contract dispute
full_text_en:
Qiu Yuliang et al. v. The People's Insurance Company (Group) of China Limited, Guanyun Sub-Branch et al. — dispute over accidental injury insurance contract

[Ruling Summary]

The teaching environment and activity facilities of a school must meet safety requirements to ensure that students' life and health are not harmed. If the school is liable for compensation for damage to a student's right to life and health due to reasons attributable to the school, and such liability falls under the insured campus liability insurance, the insurance company shall pay compensation on behalf of the school in accordance with the insurance contract. Where a school enters into a humanitarian aid compensation agreement with a parent on the condition of exempting its own liability, such agreement should be primarily characterized as compensatory in nature, rather than serving to exempt the insurance company from its liability. When the school is negligent in claiming insurance compensation, the victim's right to claim under the insurance policy shall not be deprived based on such an agreement.

Plaintiffs: Qiu Yuliang, male, 44 years old, residing in Guanyun County, Jiangsu Province.

Plaintiffs: Bian Guanglin, female, 46 years old, residing in Guanyun County, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant: The People's Insurance Company (Group) of China Limited, Guanyun Sub-Branch, domiciled at: West Shengli Road, Yishan Town, Guanyun County, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant: The People's Insurance Company (Group) of China Limited, Jiangsu Provincial Branch, domiciled at: Changjiang Road, Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province.

Third Party: Jiangsu Guanyun Senior High School, domiciled at: West Jianshe Road, Yishan Town, Guanyun County, Jiangsu Province.

Third Party: Education Department of Jiangsu Province, domiciled at: West Beijing Road, Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province.

The plaintiffs, Qiu Yuliang and Bian Guanglin, filed a lawsuit with the Guanyun County People's Court of Jiangsu Province against the defendant, The People's Insurance Company (Group) of China Limited, Guanyun Sub-Branch (hereinafter referred to as PICC Guanyun Sub-Branch), and the third party, Jiangsu Guanyun Senior High School, regarding a dispute over an accidental injury insurance contract. Subsequently, upon the plaintiffs' application, the court lawfully added The People's Insurance Company (Group) of China Limited, Jiangsu Provincial Branch (hereinafter referred to as PICC Jiangsu Provincial Branch) and the third party, the Education Department of Jiangsu Province, as parties to the proceedings.

The plaintiffs, Qiu Yuliang and Bian Guanglin, alleged: Qiu Chuang was a second-year senior high school student at Guanyun Senior High School and resided at the school dormitory. On the morning of January 6, 2013, at approximately 5:50 a.m., Qiu Chuang went to the classroom for morning self-study. The homeroom teacher organized the class to run on the playground. During the run, Qiu Chuang suddenly fell. He was taken to the county hospital at 6:25 a.m., unconscious, with no pulse or heart sounds, and was pronounced dead at 7:30 a.m. According to investigation, the education department had purchased student personal accidental injury campus liability insurance for Qiu Chuang. Pursuant to relevant laws and regulations, the third party, Guanyun Senior High School, should provide relevant evidence for the claim and assist the plaintiffs in claiming against the defendant, PICC Guanyun Sub-Branch. However, the third party failed to cooperate and shifted responsibility. The plaintiffs now file this lawsuit, requesting the court to order the defendant, PICC Jiangsu Provincial Branch, to pay RMB 300,000 in campus liability insurance proceeds, and the defendant, PICC Guanyun Sub-Branch, to pay RMB 7,500 in student and child accidental injury insurance proceeds.

The defendant, PICC Guanyun Sub-Branch, argued: The plaintiffs need to provide further evidence to prove that liability insurance was purchased from this company. PICC Guanyun Sub-Branch is not the tortfeasor in the death incident and has no insurance contract relationship with the plaintiffs; it is not the counterparty to the contract. There is no legal basis for claiming RMB 300,000 in insurance compensation under a contract action. The plaintiffs' son died due to his own reasons, which has no connection whatsoever to the school. The school bears no fault or negligence. The school, out of humanitarian considerations, has already compensated the plaintiffs RMB 150,000, and the plaintiffs have promised not to claim any further compensation from or sue the school. Since they have waived their right of action, the court should dismiss the lawsuit. In summary, the defendant requests the court to ascertain the facts and dismiss the claim or lawsuit according to law. Regarding the student and child accidental injury insurance, the plaintiffs' claim materials have been submitted to the insurance company, which will handle the matter according to law.

The defendant, PICC Jiangsu Provincial Branch, argued: Same opinion as PICC Guanyun Sub-Branch.

The third party, Jiangsu Guanyun Senior High School, argued: Regarding the campus liability insurance involved in this case, the school is not the policyholder. The plaintiffs' request for evidence has no legal basis. The third party requests the dismissal of their claims.

The third party, the Education Department of Jiangsu Province, did not submit a defense.

The Guanyun County People's Court of Jiangsu Province found the following facts at first instance:

1.  At approximately 6:00 a.m. on January 6, 2013, Qiu Chuang fell to the ground while participating in a running activity organized by his class. He was rushed to Guanyun County People's Hospital for resuscitation. The medical history record stated: "Brought to the hospital by the teacher by car at 6:25, about ten minutes after falling while running... Pronounced dead at 7:30. Diagnosis: Sudden death (out-of-hospital death)." Qiu Chuang was cremated on January 24, 2013, and his permanent residence was cancelled on February 7, 2013. The deceased, Qiu Chuang, was born on October 11, 1994. He was a registered student in Class 30, Second Year Senior High School, at Jiangsu Guanyun Senior High School. The plaintiffs, Qiu Yuliang and Bian Guanglin, are Qiu Chuang's parents.

2.  On January 24, 2013, the plaintiffs (Party B) and the third party, Jiangsu Guanyun Senior High School (Party A), signed an agreement stating: "Parties A and B confirm that Party B's son, Qiu Chuang, died accidentally due to his own reasons. Party A bears no responsibility for his death. Considering that he was a student of the school and Party B's family is in financial difficulty, Party A, out of care and humanitarian aid, pays a lump sum of RMB 150,000 to Party B. Party B and its close relatives shall not claim any further compensation or reimbursement from Party A for any rights arising from Qiu Chuang's death, nor apply for arbitration or initiate litigation." The plaintiffs have received the said RMB 150,000 from the third party, Jiangsu Guanyun Senior High School.

3.  It was further found: The third party, the Education Department of Jiangsu Province, as the policyholder, took out a School (Campus) Liability Insurance (2007 Edition) with the defendant, PICC Jiangsu Provincial Branch. The insurance premium was paid by the Jiangsu Provincial People's Government through fiscal means to the defendant. The insured are ordinary educational institutions established with the approval of relevant state departments within Jiangsu Province (including primary schools, middle schools, etc.). The cumulative compensation limit per person per year for personal injury is RMB 300,000. The incident occurred within the insurance period of this policy.

4.  It was also found: Qiu Chuang's guardian, as the policyholder, purchased a Student and Child Accidental Injury Insurance policy from the defendant, PICC Guanyun Sub-Branch, for Qiu Chuang. The insurance period commenced at 00:00 on September 1, 2012, and ended at 24:00 on August 31, 2013. The insurance coverage for accidental death, disability, or burns, and death from illness provided a sum insured of RMB 7,500 per person.

The Guanyun County People's Court held at first instance:

I. Regarding the Student and Child Accidental Injury Insurance. The insurance contract for Student and Child Accidental Injury Insurance, entered into between Qiu Chuang's guardian and the defendant, PICC Guanyun Sub-Branch, with Qiu Chuang as the insured and Qiu Chuang's legal heirs as the beneficiaries, represents the true intention of both parties, does not violate relevant legal provisions, is legally valid, and should be protected. The sum insured for accidental death, disability, or burns, and death from illness under the insurance coverage is RMB 7,500 per person. Qiu Chuang's death occurred on January 6, 2013, within the insurance period of this policy, and falls within the coverage of this insurance. The defendant, PICC Guanyun Sub-Branch, should pay insurance proceeds of RMB 7,500 to Qiu Chuang's legal heirs (the two plaintiffs in this case) in accordance with the contract terms.

II. Regarding the School (Campus) Liability Insurance (2007 Edition) involved in this case. The insurance contract for School (Campus) Liability Insurance (2007 Edition), entered into between the third party, the Education Department of Jiangsu Province, as the policyholder, and the defendant, PICC Jiangsu Provincial Branch, with the insured being ordinary educational institutions established with the approval of relevant state departments (including the third party, Jiangsu Guanyun Senior High School), represents the true intention of both parties, does not violate relevant legal provisions, is legally valid, and should be protected. The insurance coverage provides that during the insurance period, within the territory of the People's Republic of China (excluding Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan), during the insured's school activities or activities uniformly organized or arranged by the insured, if personal injury to a student arises due to the insured's negligence or fault under circumstances stipulated in the insurance clauses, and the insured is legally liable for economic compensation, the insurer shall be responsible for compensation in accordance with the insurance contract terms.

III. Regarding whether Jiangsu Guanyun Senior High School should bear responsibility for Qiu Chuang's death. The agreement signed between the plaintiffs and the third party, Jiangsu Guanyun Senior High School, stated that Qiu Chuang died accidentally due to his own reasons and that the school bore no responsibility for his death. The court, exercising its authority, obtained the inquiry records made by the public security authorities with Qiu Chuang's teachers and classmates after his death. These records show that on the day of Qiu Chuang's death, January 6, 2013, at around 6:00 a.m., He Dalian, the homeroom teacher of Qiu Chuang's class, agreed for the entire class to go downstairs, assemble, and run on the school playground. At that time, it was still dark. He Dalian used his car headlights to illuminate the running area, and the students had not yet had breakfast. During the run, at the junction of the basketball court and the plastic track on the sports field, there was a curbstone. A student in the class, Zhu Jinhui, tripped over it, and shortly thereafter, Qiu Chuang fell to the ground. The school's unified running activities were scheduled after the first two class periods in the morning. The court held that He Dalian, as the homeroom teacher, when organizing student activities outside the school's unified running schedule, should exercise a duty of prudent care regarding the venue, facilities, and whether the students' physical condition was suitable for participating in the relevant activities. Considering the above circumstances, the outdoor activity was held at an inappropriate time, and the venue facilities where the students were active posed a safety hazard. He Dalian failed to fulfill his duty of care in this regard. As a teacher of Jiangsu Guanyun Senior High School, He Dalian's teaching-related activities at the school constitute an act in the course of employment. The corresponding consequences should be borne by Jiangsu Guanyun Senior High School. Therefore, Jiangsu Guanyun Senior High School should bear corresponding responsibility for Qiu Chuang's death. Since no autopsy was performed after Qiu Chuang's death, the plaintiffs and Jiangsu Guanyun Senior High School were not the entities qualified to determine whether Qiu Chuang died accidentally due to his own reasons, nor were they the entities qualified to determine whether Jiangsu Guanyun Senior High School should bear responsibility in the matter of Qiu Chuang's death. Accordingly, the court does not recognize the relevant part of the agreement signed between the plaintiffs and Jiangsu Guanyun Senior High School. Based on the circumstances of this case and the situation on the day of Qiu Chuang's death, the court determines the proportion of compensation liability to be borne by Jiangsu Guanyun Senior High School in the matter of Qiu Chuang's death to be 50%.

Regarding the exemption clause for mental distress damages appearing in the School (Campus) Liability Insurance Clauses (2007 Edition). Since the defendant failed to provide relevant evidence proving that it had fulfilled its explicit explanation obligation, this clause shall have no effect. According to the applicable calculation standards for compensation for personal injury, the losses of the plaintiffs involved in this case include: death compensation of RMB 650,760 (RMB 32,538/year × 20 years), mental distress damages of RMB 50,000, funeral expenses of RMB 25,639.50 (RMB 51,279/year ÷ 2), and other reasonable expenses such as transportation, accommodation, and lost work for relatives attending to the funeral arrangements, which are determined at RMB 1,500. The total of the above losses is RMB 727,899.50. Jiangsu Guanyun Senior High School shall bear 50% of the compensation liability, i.e., RMB 363,949.75.

IV. Regarding the School (Campus) Liability Insurance involved in this case, the compensation liability that the insured, Jiangsu Guanyun Senior High School, should bear to the plaintiffs for their losses has been determined. However, the insured, Jiangsu Guanyun Senior High School, has been negligent in claiming the insurance proceeds from the insurer, PICC Jiangsu Provincial Branch. Therefore, the plaintiffs have the right to directly claim the insurance proceeds from the insurer, PICC Jiangsu Provincial Branch, for the part of compensation they are entitled to receive. The defendants' argument that the two plaintiffs are not the proper parties in this case is not accepted. In view of the fact that liability insurance is insurance with the insured's liability for compensation to a third party as the subject matter, the compensation liability of RMB 363,949.75 that the insured, Jiangsu Guanyun Senior High School, should bear to the plaintiffs shall, in accordance with the insurance contract, be paid by the insurer, PICC Jiangsu Provincial Branch, to the plaintiffs as insurance proceeds up to RMB 300,000.

In conclusion, the Guanyun County People's Court, pursuant to Article 60 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 2, 17, and 65 of the Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 1, 17, 18, 27, and 29 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases Involving Compensation for Personal Injury, and Article 144 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on November 6, 2014:

1.  The defendant, The People's Insurance Company (Group) of China Limited, Guanyun Sub-Branch, shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, compensate the plaintiffs, Qiu Yuliang and Bian Guanglin, with insurance proceeds of RMB 7,500.

2.  The defendant, The People's Insurance Company (Group) of China Limited, Jiangsu Provincial Branch, shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, compensate the plaintiffs, Qiu Yuliang and Bian Guanglin, with insurance proceeds of RMB 300,000.

3.  The plaintiffs' other claims are dismissed.

PICC Guanyun Sub-Branch, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Lianyungang Intermediate People's Court, arguing: (1) This case does not fall within the insurance coverage of the accident insurance or the campus liability insurance. Accident insurance covers non-illness accidental events. Campus liability insurance covers the compensation liability that the insured should bear according to law. The first-instance court's finding that Qiu Chuang's fall was related to the school, and its subsequent conclusion that the fall directly caused his death, leading to the inference of a causal link between school management and Qiu Chuang's death, is clearly erroneous. The hospital diagnosed Qiu Chuang as "sudden death," not death directly caused by falling during morning exercises. According to common knowledge, only illness can cause sudden death. The plaintiffs also subsequently acknowledged that Qiu Chuang died due to his own problems, which does not constitute an accident. Therefore, this case is not within the scope of insurance coverage. The "Explanation Regarding the Accidental Death and Aftermath Handling of Student Qiu Chuang" shows that the Guanyun County Education Bureau did not find the school at fault. The public security authorities also did not find the school at fault. The court's reliance solely on the inquiry records from the public security authorities to find the school 50% liable clearly lacks factual and legal basis. (2) The first-instance judgment ordering PICC Jiangsu Provincial Branch to pay RMB 300,000 in compensation is not compensation liability that the school should legally bear. The plaintiffs and the school had the right to conduct equal negotiations and reach an agreement regarding compensation for Qiu Chuang's death, and they clearly stated that after receiving RMB 150,000, they waived all rights arising from Qiu Chuang's death. Since the insured's (school's) compensation liability was extinguished after paying RMB 150,000, even if the incident falls within the insurance coverage, the insurer need only bear compensation liability within the limit of RMB 150,000. (3) The first-instance judgment ordering PICC Jiangsu Provincial Branch to pay RMB 300,000 clearly exceeds the amount of compensation the plaintiffs are legally entitled to receive. The first-instance judgment determined that the school, as the insured, should pay the plaintiffs RMB 363,949.75. The RMB 150,000 already paid by the school, though termed "compensation," is in fact a payment for damages. Even if Qiu Chuang's death was the school's liability, this amount should be deducted; otherwise, it results in double recovery. (4) This case does not fall within the circumstances stipulated in Article 65 of the Insurance Law where the insured is negligent in exercising its right to claim. The plaintiffs are not proper parties in this case. After receiving the compensation from the school, they waived their right to sue the school and therefore have no right to subrogation against PICC Jiangsu Provincial Branch. (5) PICC Jiangsu Provincial Branch has fulfilled its obligation of explicit explanation. If this case falls within the insurance coverage, the mental distress damages involved should be exempt. The school knew that the "curbstone" facility could cause students to fall but continued to use it; damage caused thereby also falls under the exemption. When PICC Jiangsu Provincial Branch signed the contract with the Education Department of Jiangsu Province, it explained the insurance clauses and fulfilled the explicit explanation obligation regarding the exemption clauses. Therefore, mental distress damages should not be compensated. In summary, the appellant requests the appellate court to ascertain the facts and dismiss the plaintiffs' claims according to law.

The appellees, Qiu Yuliang and Bian Guanglin, jointly argued in defense: The appellant, PICC Guanyun Sub-Branch, can only appeal against the civil liability imposed under the first judgment item of the first instance. Matters beyond that are not within the scope of review by the appellate court. Its claims regarding the effective content of its appeal are also untenable. This case involves two types of insurance: accident insurance and campus liability insurance. Therefore, the first-instance judgment found the facts clearly, had sufficient evidence, and was legal and just. The appellees request the appellate court to affirm the judgment.

The original defendant, PICC Jiangsu Provincial Branch, stated its opinion consistent with the appellant, PICC Guanyun Sub-Branch's appeal opinion.

The third party, Guanyun Senior High School, stated: The first-instance judgment's finding that the school was at fault lacks factual and legal basis. The failure to recognize the validity of the agreement reached between the school and the student's parents also lacks legal basis. The school did not appeal only due to its special relationship with the student's family. The case is to be decided by the court according to law.

The third party, the Education Department of Jiangsu Province, stated: We agree with PICC Guanyun Sub-Branch's views. According to relevant provisions of the Tort Law, no guardianship relationship exists between a school and its students; only an educational administrative relationship exists. Moreover, for torts committed against persons with limited capacity for civil conduct, the school should apply the principle of fault liability as per the Tort Law.

The Lianyungang Intermediate People's Court, upon hearing the appeal, confirmed the facts found at first instance.

The Lianyungang Intermediate People's Court held on appeal:

The insurance contract entered into between the third party, the Education Department of Jiangsu Province, and the original defendant, PICC Jiangsu Provincial Branch, as well as the insurance contract entered into between the appellees, Qiu Yuliang and Bian Guanglin, and the appellant, PICC Guanyun Sub-Branch, represent the true intention of the parties, do not violate mandatory provisions of laws and regulations, are legally valid, and both parties shall perform their obligations accordingly.

The fact that Qiu Chuang fell and died despite rescue efforts during a physical activity uniformly organized by the school is objectively existent. Neither the appellees, Qiu Yuliang and Bian Guanglin, nor Guanyun Senior High School are specialized medical technical institutions or judicial forensic medical identification institutions qualified to determine the cause of an individual's death. The medical records in this case do not reflect what illness caused Qiu Chuang's death. The appellant, PICC Guanyun Sub-Branch, argued that the agreement between Qiu Yuliang, Bian Guanglin, and Guanyun Senior High School had determined that "Qiu Chuang died accidentally due to his own reasons," but this agreement lacks professional medical basis. Therefore, the appellant PICC Guanyun Sub-Branch's argument that "Qiu Chuang died accidentally due to his own reasons" is not adopted.

Article 3 of the "Campus Liability Insurance Clauses" of the insurance contract entered into between the Education Department of Jiangsu Province, as the policyholder, and PICC Jiangsu Provincial Branch stipulates that within the territory of the People's Republic of China (excluding Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan), during the insured's school activities or activities uniformly organized or arranged by the insured, if personal injury to a student arises due to the insured's negligence or fault under circumstances stipulated in the insurance clauses, the insurer shall be responsible for compensating the economic compensation liability that the insured should legally bear, in accordance with the insurance contract terms. In this case, upon review, according to regulations, the school's uniformly organized physical activities were scheduled after the first two class periods in the morning. However, He Dalian, a teacher of the insured, Guanyun Senior High School, assembled the entire class of students who had not yet eaten breakfast on the school playground when it was still dark, used his car headlights to illuminate the area for students to run, resulting in student Zhu Jinhui tripping and Qiu Chuang falling and dying despite rescue efforts. The insured, Guanyun Senior High School, may organize extracurricular physical activities outside of teaching hours, at an appropriate time and after students have completed warm-up exercises. However, based on the above circumstances, the teacher of Guanyun Senior High School caused students to engage in running activities at an inappropriate time for outdoor activities and when the students had not yet warmed up, thereby failing to fulfill its duty of care. He Dalian's relevant teaching activities at the school constitute acts in the course of employment, and the corresponding consequences shall be borne by Guanyun Senior High School.

Regarding the issue of whether the appellee, Qiu Yuliang, after entering into a humanitarian assistance agreement with Guanyun Senior High School, has the right to claim insurance compensation from PICC Jiangsu Branch in accordance with the "Campus Liability Insurance Clauses," the court of second instance held that the 150,000 yuan paid by Guanyun Senior High School to Qiu Yuliang was explicitly designated as a humanitarian assistance payment in the agreement in question, and was not compensation in nature. The agreement reached between the parties did not address the issue of liability for compensation or the issue of insurance claim rights, meaning Qiu Yuliang did not expressly waive his right to insurance compensation. Pursuant to Article 2 of the Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China, Qiu Yuliang and Bian Guanglin are entitled to assert their rights against PICC Jiangsu Branch.

Regarding the appellant, PICC Guanyun Branch's contention that mental distress compensation arising from Qiu Chuang's death should not be covered by insurance compensation according to the insurance clauses, the court of second instance, upon review, held that the amount of compensation determined by the court of first instance to be borne by the school was 363,949.75 yuan. Even if the 50,000 yuan in mental distress compensation were deducted, the remaining amount would be 313,949.75 yuan, which is still higher than the 300,000 yuan in insurance compensation adjudicated by the court of first instance. The court of first instance's decision that PICC Jiangsu Branch bear insurance liability of 300,000 yuan has a contractual basis and complies with the relevant provisions of the Insurance Law.

In summary, the facts found by the court of first instance were clear, and the outcome was appropriate. The grounds of appeal raised by the appellant, PICC Guanyun Branch, are all untenable. The Lianyungang Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with Article 170, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on July 1, 2015:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

This judgment is final.
